per_case.playbook: Isolate 192.168.100.46 from the network immediately. Block outbound connections to 192.168.100.5. Investigate the host for malware/botnet implants, inspect the port 3456 reverse channel for C2 communication, preserve forensic images, review credential usage (given the privilege-gain classification), and audit 192.168.100.5 for successful compromise. Correlate with threat intel for the botnet signature.

Isolate 192.168.100.5 from the network immediately. Preserve a forensic disk/image image and memory dump. Hunt for and remove the malware/C2 implant responsible for the brute-force to 192.168.100.3 and the beaconing from internal hosts (192.168.100.46, etc.). Block outbound connections to 192.168.100.3 and to the beaconing internal hosts. Investigate the initial compromise vector and pivot to identify any other hosts that beacon to 192.168.100.5.

ISOLATE_HOST - Immediately isolate 192.168.100.55 from the network. Investigate for initial access vector and credential theft (the alert classification is 'Attempted Administrator Privilege Gain'). Block outbound connections to 192.168.100.3 and audit that host for signs of compromise. Rotate credentials for any accounts that authenticated from 192.168.100.55. Perform forensic imaging before remediation, then rebuild from known-good baseline.

Isolate 192.168.100.7 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic images, perform memory and disk forensics, identify the malware family beaconing to 192.168.100.3:565, block outbound traffic to 192.168.100.3 at the firewall, and hunt for lateral movement to other hosts on the 192.168.100.0/24 subnet. Investigate 192.168.100.3 as the internal C2 peer.

BLOCK the external IP 162.208.20.178 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter immediately. Investigate the 6 internal hosts (especially 192.168.10.5, 192.168.10.9, 192.168.10.8) for malware/compromise and isolate them, as they are the beaconing sources. Block C2 egress, capture any payloads, and hunt for the malware family responsible for the beaconing.

BLOCK the external IP 178.255.83.1 at the perimeter firewall/IPS immediately. Additionally, investigate the 12 internal source hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .12, .14, .15, .16, .17, .19, .50, .51, .25) for compromise, as they are beaconing to this C2 and should be isolated and forensically examined. Block outbound connections to 178.255.83.1 from all internal hosts.
No action required. This is benign DNS server traffic. Continue routine monitoring; no isolation or IP block warranted.

Isolate 192.168.10.14 from the network immediately. Preserve forensic images before rebuilding. Block outbound DNS to 192.168.10.3:53 and monitor internal hosts that beacon to 192.168.10.14 (especially 192.168.10.8) for lateral movement. Hunt for the malware family responsible for the DNS beacon and C2 receiver behavior, and review firewall/EDR telemetry for the implant's full activity timeline.

No action required. Mark the FLOW-002 alert as a benign heuristic false positive. Optionally baseline the host's DNS query rate to reduce future false positives; only escalate to ISOLATE_HOST if DNS payloads grow abnormally large (tunneling) or if endpoint events/malare indicators appear.

BLOCK the external C2 IP 205.174.165.73 at the perimeter firewall/IPS immediately. In parallel, ISOLATE and forensically image the 6 internal hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .14, .15, .25) that are beaconing to it, hunt for the delivering trojan/malware, and rotate any credentials or secrets on those hosts.

BLOCK the external IP 23.50.75.27 at the perimeter firewall/egress filtering immediately. Investigate the 11 internal source hosts (192.168.10.5–192.168.10.25) for malware/compromise, as they are the beaconing endpoints. Block at egress, capture sample flows for forensic analysis, and initiate host remediation on the compromised internal machines.

BLOCK 23.61.187.27 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter immediately. Block outbound port 80 to this IP from all internal hosts. Investigate the 12 source hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .12, .14, .15, .16, .17, .19, .25, .50, .51) for malware/compromise and isolate as needed. Correlate with threat intel once API access is restored.

Block 72.167.239.239 at the perimeter firewall/IPS immediately and add it to the threat intelligence blocklist. Investigate the 11 internal source hosts (192.168.10.5, .8, .9, .12, .14, .15, .16, .17, .19, .25, .51) for malware/compromise and isolate them as secondary actions. Correlate with DNS logs to identify the resolved domain behind this C2 IP.

BLOCK 72.21.91.29 at the perimeter firewall/egress filter immediately. Concurrently isolate and forensically image the 13 internal source hosts (192.168.10.3, .8, .9, .12, .14, .15, .16, .17, .19, .25, .50, .51, etc.) that are beaconing to this C2, and hunt for the malware family responsible. Add the IP to the blocklist and monitor for any new destinations or C2 infrastructure tied to the same beaconing campaign.
